clue.text: Very successful, when in mid-life, weathering storms here?

parts.note: a roaring success is a very successful one, so roaring can mean thriving
someone in their forties is in middle age

explanation.surface: A thriving middle-aged person is asked where they ride out life's storms.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests someone weathering a mid-life crisis; the definition is a place, the stormy ocean latitudes.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the windy southern ocean latitudes between forty and fifty degrees, notorious among sailors for gales.

clue.text: Verbal report about debut

parts.note: re is Latin for concerning, so it means about
a debutante's debut is her presentation at court

explanation.surface: A spoken account of someone's first appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: A representation is a formal statement or account made to an authority, often spoken.

clue.text: A raise in subscription I have to support is offensive

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath the rest
in a down clue raising a word turns it upwards, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a sub is short for a subscription
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A rise in membership fees that I must back is insulting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raise' turns SUB upside down in this down entry to give BUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Abusive means insulting or offensive in speech or treatment.

clue.text: Key perhaps found, or secreted by woman?

indicators.note: something secreted by a person is hidden on them, so it sits inside the woman's name

parts.note: Ivy is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A key is found, or hidden by a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' suggests a door key; piano keys were traditionally made of this material.
explanation.definitionFit: Piano keys were traditionally faced with ivory, so a white key is an example.

clue.text: Turn jolly, without becoming silly

parts.note: a go is a turn in a game
a jolly is old slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM
less means without, as in a meal less pudding

explanation.surface: Someone turns merry, without becoming foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' is a Royal Marine (RM), a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Gormless is a British word for stupid or lacking sense, which is silly.

clue.text: Avocet breaks into a series of notes

indicators.note: a bird that breaks is broken up, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wading bird bursts into song.
explanation.definitionFit: An octave is the run of eight notes in a musical scale.

clue.text: Change the voltage in new trams for resort

indicators.note: in puts the new letter inside the rearranged words
to re-sort is to sort again, so the words trams for are rearranged

explanation.surface: Electrical work on new trams heading for a seaside resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' is read as re-sort, sorting again; the seaside sense is the surface's decoy. 'in' sets N within the rearranged letters TRASFORM.
explanation.definitionFit: A transformer steps voltage up or down, so to transform is to change voltage.

clue.text: Digest eastern holy book

parts.note: pi is schoolboy slang for pious or holy
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: A summary of an Oriental scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digest' suggests eating; it is a summary.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitome is a summary or abstract, as a digest is.

clue.text: Finance house after 500 for shady deal

indicators.note: after places the firm behind the slang sum

parts.note: a monkey is British slang for five hundred pounds
a finance house is a business or firm

explanation.surface: A finance firm takes five hundred pounds for a crooked deal.
explanation.walkthrough: MONKEY is British slang for £500, as printed in the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Monkey business is mischievous or underhand dealing, an idiom for trickery.

clue.text: PR a cult to manipulate to become a rich man

indicators.note: to manipulate is to handle and rework, so the preceding letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A public relations man exploits a cult in order to get rich.
explanation.definitionFit: A plutocrat is a person whose power comes from great wealth, a rich man.

clue.text: Friend in Spain is fighter in a ring

indicators.note: the word in sets the fighter inside the a-and-ring pair

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O
a MiG is a Russian fighter aircraft

explanation.surface: A Spanish pal turns out to be a boxer in the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is the Spanish word for a friend, borrowed into English.

clue.text: Improve understanding of European change, losing little time

indicators.note: losing says that the short time is dropped from the word for change

parts.note: to modify something is to change it
a mo is a moment, a little time

explanation.surface: Learning about European change improves one's grasp, though it takes a moment less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' leaves DIFY. The full stop after 'Improve' in the held text was a smudge on the page, so the definition runs across it.
explanation.definitionFit: To edify is to instruct someone for their moral or intellectual benefit, raising their knowledge.

clue.text: Hot soup for farm animals

parts.note: a hot wire is live, carrying electric current
stock is the broth used as a soup base

explanation.surface: Hot soup is served to the animals on the farm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot' suggests temperature; here it is the electrical sense, as a live wire.
explanation.definitionFit: Livestock is the collective term for cattle, sheep and other animals raised on a farm.

clue.text: It's wise to take this train

definitions.meaning: a cryptic nod to the advice that taking some physical activity is wise
to train is to drill or work out

explanation.definitionFit: Exercise is physical activity, and to exercise is to train the body or drill troops.

clue.text: Include this sort of clue in TV programme

parts.note: to count someone in is to include them
the clue itself is a down clue in the grid

explanation.surface: A setter is told to put this kind of clue in a television show.
explanation.walkthrough: Countdown is a long-running British TV word and numbers game show.
explanation.definitionFit: Countdown is a British daytime television quiz show of letters and numbers.

clue.text: Buffalo Bill touring state in zany show

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the showman's surname goes round the state

parts.note: William Cody was the showman known as Buffalo Bill
ME is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Maine

explanation.surface: Buffalo Bill's Wild West show tours a state with a crazy act.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedy is a humorous play or show, which may well be zany.

clue.text: Offering a deposit, wanting place over the border

indicators.note: in a down clue over puts the first piece above the second
wanting means lacking, so the word place is cut down to its abbreviation

parts.note: edging is a border, as on fabric

explanation.surface: Someone offers a deposit, hoping for a place across the border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' trims PLACE to PL, its usual abbreviation; 'over' stacks PL above EDGING in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To pledge is to give something as security, so pledging is handing over a deposit.

clue.text: Its contents may have been bagged for would-be drinker

definitions.text: Its contents may have been bagged for would-be drinker

parts.words: Its contents may have been bagged for would-be drinker
parts.note: the drink inside it was made from leaves sold in little bags, served to someone wanting a hot drink

explanation.definitionFit: A small cup for drinking tea, the brew often made with a teabag.

clue.text: Sick parrot, one you may expect, to fly here

definitions.text: you may expect, to fly here

indicators.note: a sick parrot is out of sorts, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: An ailing parrot is expected to be flown out.
explanation.definitionFit: An airport is where passengers board planes and fly from.

clue.text: Torch carried by two sweethearts? The first falls short

indicators.note: the first of the two lovers' words is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a flame is a lover, and so is a beau
a flame is a lover, and so is a beau

explanation.surface: Two lovers carry a torch for each other, but the first fails to keep it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The first falls short' leaves FLAM. 'Carry a torch' is the lovesick idiom the surface leans on, while 'Torch' itself is the plain definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A flambeau is a flaming torch, especially one made of thick wicks dipped in wax.

clue.text: Emerge as a name in English china

indicators.note: in places the short name inside the friend

parts.note: china plate is rhyming slang for mate, a friend

explanation.surface: A name comes to light in English porcelain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'china' is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate, mate.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to issue or flow out from a source, which is to emerge.

clue.text: University in Milan turning out graduates

indicators.note: in puts the university letter within the rearranged city
turning out suggests turning inside out, so the city's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A university in Milan produces graduates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning out' rearranges MILAN into ALMNI, and 'in' places U inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Alumni are former students who have graduated from a school or university.

clue.text: Choked, as daughter falls behind means to speed up progress

indicators.note: falls behind places the daughter's letter after the engine control

parts.note: the throttle controls an engine's fuel and so its speed

explanation.surface: A driver chokes as the daughter falls behind and they put their foot down.
explanation.definitionFit: To throttle is to strangle, so throttled means choked.

clue.text: I first crawled, perhaps, to religious teacher

parts.note: the crawl is a swimming stroke, so one who crawled swam

explanation.surface: Someone recalls first crawling before going to a guru.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I first crawled, perhaps' reads as 'I swam'; the answer is that phrase with the words inverted, SWAM then I.
explanation.definitionFit: A swami is a Hindu holy man and teacher of religion.

clue.text: In flight, it goes up and down

definitions.text: In flight, it goes up and down

parts.words: In flight, it goes up and down
parts.note: a flight here is a set of steps, each of which people climb and descend

explanation.definitionFit: A stair is one step in a flight of steps that people walk up and down.

clue.text: Thumb small volume in old bindings

indicators.note: in places the book's abbreviation between the two covering letters

parts.note: old is abbreviated O, and bindings puts one O as a cover on each side
vol is the short form of volume

explanation.surface: Someone leafs through a little book in an old binding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thumb' suggests leafing through the book; it is an architectural moulding.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovolo is a convex rounded moulding, also known in joinery as a thumb moulding.

clue.text: Female domestic and a manservant taking time off in west London area

parts.note: a maid is a female domestic servant

indicators.note: taking off means removing, so the time letter comes away from the servant

parts.note: a valet is a gentleman's manservant

explanation.surface: A maid and a valet take time off to go to west London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' drops T from VALET, leaving VALE. Maida Vale is a residential district of west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Maida Vale is an affluent residential district in the west of London, near Paddington.

clue.text: Rules of procedure for coping with classes

parts.note: to stand something is to put up with it, so standing means coping with
orders are ranks or classes, as in the lower orders

explanation.surface: Rules govern how to manage teaching classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Classes' suggests school; it means ranks of society.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing orders are the permanent rules governing the conduct of a parliament or meeting.
